resources.string: Mobility Lens
Mobility Lens
Six things that make mobile app design different from desktop design.
Input and Interaction
On a phone you\'re tapping and swiping with your finger, sometimes with just one hand, instead of using a mouse and a full keyboard like on a computer.
Make buttons at least 48dp tall so they\'re easy to tap, and don\'t put important actions in the corners where a thumb can\'t reach one handed.
Screen Size, Orientation, and Density
Phone screens are small and can flip between portrait and landscape at any time, and they come in a ton of different sizes. Computer monitors are usually bigger and just stay put.
Test the layout in both portrait and landscape, and use dp units instead of fixed pixel sizes so it doesn\'t break on a different screen density.
Lifecycle and Resource Constraints
The phone\'s OS can shut down your app at any point to save battery or memory, so you can\'t assume it just keeps running like a program on a laptop would.
Save form input or scroll position with rememberSaveable or a ViewModel, so the user doesn\'t lose progress if the app gets killed in the background.
Context Awareness
Phones know a lot about what\'s going on around them, like your location, movement, and camera, stuff a regular computer usually doesn\'t have access to.
A food delivery app can use GPS to auto fill the user\'s address instead of making them type it in manually every time.
Usage Patterns
People check their phones for quick things throughout the day and get interrupted a lot, versus sitting at a desktop for one long focused session.
Let the user check a delivery status or a bank balance in one or two taps instead of forcing them through a multi step flow every time they open the app.
Security and Privacy Expectations
Phones carry a lot of personal info and ask for permission each time before touching something sensitive, unlike desktops which usually just trust the app by default.
If the user denies the camera permission, still let them upload a photo from their gallery instead of the feature just breaking.
